name: Fujian Tulou — Fusheng Lou
scaleNote: 1 stud per metre. A 77.42 m ring at 1 stud/m is 77 studs across, which is the smallest circle on which arrangeOn does not collapse neighbours onto the same studs.

diameter.source: Wikipedia, Fujian tulou: Fusheng Lou's 'diameter was measured at 77.42 meters', the largest circular tulou.

wallBase.source: Wikipedia, Fujian tulou: wall thickness 'decreases with height' from approximately two metres at bottom to one metre at top.

wallTop.source: Wikipedia, Fujian tulou: '...from approximately two meters at bottom to one meter at top.'

height.source: Wikipedia, Fujian tulou: Heguilou measures '21.5 meters' in height -- the only height the article gives for any tulou, and Heguilou is RECTANGULAR, not the circular Fusheng Lou built here.

eaves.source: Wikipedia, Fujian tulou: eaves typically 'extend about two meters'.

note:
A COMMUNAL EARTH BUILDING IS THE CLOSEST THING ON THIS LIST TO WHAT THE PROJECT CLAIMS. A tulou is one wall, rammed in courses, enclosing a shared void -- modular, repetitive, and built by a community rather than a state. Great Zimbabwe is the other one.

THE HEIGHT IS BORROWED FROM A DIFFERENT BUILDING. 21.5 m is Heguilou's, and Heguilou is rectangular; Fusheng Lou's height is not in the article. The figure is cited with its own contradiction attached rather than quietly transplanted, because a reader deserves to know the roofline of this ring came from a building of another shape.

The wall tapers 2 m to 1 m over its height. This builds it as two concentric rings of straight runs -- `arrangeOn` bends instances, not walls, so a true circle of wall is not available and a 24-sided figure is what stands.

Der Traufring sass zuerst auf Radius 39,7 und damit ausserhalb der Mauer -- 24 schwebende Steine. Eine Traufe kragt in der Wirklichkeit genau so aus; hier muss sie auf der Mauer stehen, weil dieses Vokabular kein Kragwerk hat. Sie ist stattdessen breiter als die Mauer.
